Bolton writer Ryan Abbey lets internet control new story

16th September
By Maddie Avery Trainee Reporter

Share

0 comments

A Bolton writer is letting strangers decide his story–and it took an unexpected turn

Ryan Abbey runs WorkOfR and started The Internet Writes a Book at the beginning of September (Image: Ryan Abbey)

A Bolton writer is letting strangers decide his story–and it took an unexpected turn

A Bolton-based writer has launched an unusual literary experiment that allows members of the public to decide what happens next in a novel being written in real time online.

Ryan Abbey, who runs independent creative project WorkOfR, started The Internet Writes a Book at the beginning of September, inviting readers to take an active role in shaping the story's direction.

The project sees Ryan, who has written children's books before, publish a new instalment each day before asking followers to suggest what should happen next.

Participants have until 9am the following morning to submit ideas and vote for their favourites by liking comments.

Ryan's grandad holding one of his children's books (Image: Ryan Abbey)

The winning suggestion is then incorporated into the next chapter, leaving Ryan with the task of writing, recording and producing the next instalment before the process begins again.

Ryan said: "This is very much an experiment to see what happens when you give strangers genuine control over the direction of the story."

The concept means that while Ryan remains the author, much of the story's direction is dictated by readers, creating twists and turns that even he cannot predict.

Speaking about how the project has evolved, he said: "We're only ten days into the experiment and it's already gone somewhere I could never have planned.

"Joe began as an ordinary office worker who wanted something more from life.

"Ten days later, entirely because of suggestions from people taking part, he's discovered he may actually be a prince from a magical kingdom and is currently on his way to meet the king."

The online storytelling project is being created entirely from Bolton and will continue daily until the end of October.

Once the experiment concludes, Ryan hopes to turn the finished online story into a published book.

He said: "I'm going to do 60 days and then on the 31st October when we conclude the story, then I'm going to get the physical book in development and hopefully out within four weeks from that point."

While the project has attracted a loyal group of contributors, Ryan is encouraging more people to get involved.

He said: "The same people are coming back to continue the story, which is good, but new faces are very sparse at the moment.

"The more contributors, the more twists and turns it can bring into the story."

The experiment forms part of Ryan's wider WorkOfR project, a platform he created to connect with fellow creatives and showcase original content, including stories, films and spoken-word poetry.

Explaining the inspiration behind the initiative, Ryan said: "As far back as I can remember I've always created things whether it be stories, films, spoken word poetry but I never had a place for it because I felt like putting it under my own personal account, people didn't engage with it because they knew me as a person, but not as an artist.

"What I wanted to do is create a space, that I've called WorkOfR, that's basically a platform that just engages with people of a similar nature or people interested in the arts and we can put things on there."

The Internet Writes a Book can be followed on Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and TikTok through the WorkOfR channels, where readers can help decide what happens next in Joe's increasingly unpredictable adventure.
